note: Heli-skiing and cat skiing operations across Canada, shown in Skiing (helicat.js). Hand-edited from: the HeliCat Canada member lists (helicat.org), the catskiing.ca directory, each operator's own website and the linked articles (checked 2026-10-26). Prices: what the source showed, with its season; 'older' = an undated directory listing, check the operator for today's price. areas = BC Crown land tenure file numbers in helicat-areas.json that belong to this operator (matched by lodge location and tenure name). approx = the pin is placed roughly (town or lodge area). check = couldn't confirm it still operates.

ops.name: Whistler Heli-Skiing
ops.about: Classic day heli-skiing straight from Whistler Village, run with Whistler Blackcomb, operating for about 40 seasons.
ops.access: In Whistler Village, about 1 h 15 min drive north of Vancouver.

ops.name: Coast Range Heli-Skiing
ops.about: Small-group and private day heli-skiing in the Coast Mountains around Whistler, with longer days and more runs.
ops.access: Highway 99, north of Vancouver (Whistler and Pemberton).
ops.level: Intermediate to expert skiers and boarders

price.t: Single seat CAD $2,195 per person; private group of 4 CAD $7,260; own helicopter CAD $14,300 (per day)

ops.name: Powder Mountain Cat and Heli Skiing
ops.about: Whistler's only cat skiing, plus heli days. When helicopters can't fly the cats still go, and the area gets much more snow than Whistler Blackcomb.
ops.access: Office in Whistler Village, a few minutes from the Whistler Gondola; the cat terrain is about 20 minutes south of Whistler.
trips: Day cat skiing (6 runs guaranteed, unlimited vertical)
ops.group: Cat: 12 guests + 2 guides per cat. Heli: 4 guests + 1 guide

price.t: Cat from CAD $780 + GST; heli from CAD $2,000 + GST (per person per day)

ops.name: Phantom Heli Skiing
ops.about: Small-group day heli-skiing run by local mountain guides across the Sea to Sky corridor.
ops.access: Departures from Whistler, Squamish and downtown Vancouver. Flies with Black Tusk Helicopter, the tenure holder.
trips: Day trips from Whistler, Squamish or downtown Vancouver

ops.name: Backcountry Snowcats (Hurley Mountain Lodge)
ops.about: Cozy remote lodge, about 10 m of cold dry snow a year: colder and drier than Whistler but the same storms.
ops.access: Meet in Pemberton, about 2 h from Vancouver; snowmobile ride in to the lodge near Hurley Pass, 1 h north of Whistler.
trips: Multi-day lodge trips at Hurley Mountain Lodge

price.t: About CAD $650 to $775 per day (older listing)

ops.name: Tyax Heliskiing (TLH)
ops.about: Lakeside lodge plus two private chalets. Cold Chilcotin air meets Pacific storms, giving dry snow.
ops.access: About 3 h from Vancouver airport, transfers included. Lodge on Tyaughton Lake near Gold Bridge.
trips: Single group per helicopter, unlimited vertical

ops.name: Bella Coola Heli Sports
ops.about: One of the biggest heli-ski areas in the world, coast range peaks right above the valley.
ops.access: About a 70-minute flight from Vancouver, included.
ops.lodge: Eagle Lodge, Tweedsmuir Park Lodge, or the MV Cascadia boat

ops.name: Great Bear Heli Skiing
ops.region: Central Coast Mountains, Great Bear Rainforest
ops.base: Great Bear Lodge, Lower Dean River
ops.about: Family-run boutique lodge on the Lower Dean River, between the snowy coast and the drier Chilcotin.
ops.access: Private charter flight from Vancouver and a helicopter transfer to the lodge, organized for you.

ops.name: Northern Escape Heli-Skiing
ops.about: About 100 ft of snow a year. Snowcats take you into sheltered trees when the helicopters can't fly. Named World's Best Heli-Ski Operator 2022 to 2025 (World Ski Awards).
ops.access: Minutes from Terrace airport (30 min shuttle or heli).

ops.name: White Wilderness Heli Skiing
ops.about: Small-group heli skiing from a riverside lodge with refined lodging and meals.
ops.access: Fly Vancouver or Calgary to Terrace (about 1 h 45 min); the lodge is about 20-30 min away by road.

ops.name: Skeena Heliskiing
ops.about: Big varied terrain, from high alpine steeps to glades, from a 15,000 sq ft timber lodge on the Kispiox River.
ops.access: About 1 h 40 min drive north of Smithers airport (1.5 h from Smithers).
ops.group: Max 12 guests per week, small groups, 2 helicopters

ops.name: Skeena Cat Skiing
ops.about: Northern BC's only dedicated cat operation, cold snow at about 55.5°N.
ops.access: Fly to Terrace or Smithers, then a short helicopter flight to Base Camp, about 80 km north of Smithers.
ops.vert: Runs up to 1,200 vertical metres, up to 15 runs a day
trips: 3 and 4 day trips from Base Camp

price.t: About CAD $800 to $1,200 per day (older listing)

ops.name: Last Frontier Heliskiing (Bell 2 Lodge)
ops.about: Remote wilderness lodge on the Stewart-Cassiar Highway, huge variety: open bowls, glaciers and trees.
ops.access: About 4 h north of Terrace on Highway 37.
ops.terrain: 10,100 km² shared with Ripley Creek (largest single heli-ski area)

ops.name: Last Frontier Heliskiing (Ripley Creek, Stewart)
ops.about: Town-based lodge into the steep Coast Mountains right on the Alaska border.
ops.access: In Stewart, on the Alaska border at the end of Highway 37A.

ops.name: Gold Rush Heli Skiing
ops.region: Coast Mountains, Atlin and the Juneau Icefield
ops.about: New operation (from 2026) in BC's far northwest, cabins and a lodge looking over Atlin Lake.
ops.access: Met in Whitehorse, Yukon, then transfer to Atlin (about 2.5 h). First season 2026.
ops.terrain: 648,000 acres (Willison and Llewellyn Glaciers, Juneau Icefield)
ops.vert: Open bowls up to about 4,500 ft
ops.group: Max 8 guests, groups of 4, 2 A-Star helicopters

ops.name: Yukon Heliski
ops.region: White Pass (BC, by the Yukon and Alaska borders)
ops.about: Spring heli-skiing in the far north with long days: cabins, saloon and sauna at base.
ops.access: Transfer from Whitehorse airport (Yukon) to the base in the White Pass.

ops.name: Bearpaw Heli-Skiing
ops.region: Northern Rockies, McGregor and Dezaiko ranges
ops.about: Low-key small lodge with private rooms, mostly open gladed tree skiing.
ops.access: Fly to Prince George (about 1 h from Vancouver), then about 1 h drive east.

ops.name: Crescent Spur Heli-Skiing
ops.about: Ranch-style lodge with big open bowls and glaciers above and gladed forest below.
ops.access: About 2 h drive east of Prince George.

ops.name: Silvertip Lodge Heli-Skiing
ops.about: Remote lodge on the shore of Quesnel Lake; glaciated alpine, open terrain and natural trees.
ops.access: About a 45-minute helicopter ride from Williams Lake.

ops.name: Mike Wiegele Helicopter Skiing
ops.about: Running since 1970, one of the largest operations, with its own year-round village.
ops.access: About 2.5 h drive north of Kamloops on Highway 5.
ops.lodge: Heli Village of log chalets and estate houses, plus Albreda Lodge
ops.group: Groups of various sizes, private options
ops.level: Intermediate to expert skiers and boarders

ops.name: CMH Cariboos
ops.about: CMH's Cariboos lodge, deep in the Cariboo Mountains near Valemount.
ops.access: Near Valemount; coach from Kelowna or Calgary airports, then helicopter to the lodge.

ops.name: CMH Valemount
ops.about: CMH's road-access lodge in Valemount.
ops.access: In Valemount on Highway 5, about 1.5 h west of Jasper.
trips: Multi-day trips from a town lodge

ops.name: Cariboo Snowcat Skiing
ops.about: Day cat skiing on Mica Mountain in the Cariboos.
ops.access: Near Valemount, about 1 h drive west of Jasper, AB.
ops.vert: Usually 10,000 to 15,000 vertical feet a day

price.t: About CAD $675 to $775 per day (older listing)

ops.name: CMH Monashees
ops.about: CMH's Monashees lodge: steep tree skiing in the northern Monashees.
ops.access: Near Blue River; coach and helicopter transfer.

ops.name: Mica Heliskiing
ops.region: Selkirk, Monashee and Rocky Mountains, Kinbasket Lake
ops.about: Luxury lakeside lodge; pillow lines, fall-line tree skiing and open alpine.
ops.access: About 2 h drive north of Revelstoke.
ops.group: 4 guests + 1 guide per group, 16 guests total

ops.name: Chatter Creek
ops.about: Big Rockies tenure looking at the Columbia Icefield: tree skiing, alpine bowls and glaciers, from a 20,000 sq ft timber lodge.
ops.access: About 3 h drive from Calgary to Golden, then a helicopter flight to the lodge.

price.t: About CAD $615 to $935 per day (older listing)

ops.name: CMH Adamants
ops.about: CMH's Adamants lodge with big glaciated terrain.
ops.access: North of Revelstoke; helicopter to the lodge.

ops.name: CMH Gothics
ops.about: CMH's Gothics lodge north of Revelstoke.
ops.access: North of Revelstoke; helicopter to the lodge.

ops.name: CMH Revelstoke
ops.about: CMH's Revelstoke base, skiing the Monashees and Selkirks around town.
ops.access: In Revelstoke on the Trans-Canada Highway.
trips: Multi-day trips from a town lodge

ops.name: Selkirk Tangiers Heli Skiing
ops.about: 40+ years in Revelstoke, deep powder, old-growth forest and alpine bowls on both sides of town.
ops.access: In Revelstoke, about 2 h 15 min from Kelowna.

ops.name: Eagle Pass Heliskiing
ops.about: Small groups of 4 in the Monashees: alpine bowls, long chutes and glades.
ops.access: Revelstoke, about 1.5 h drive from Kelowna airport.

price.t: Day heli CAD $1,660 (early and late season) to $2,600 (peak), per person

ops.name: Eleven Revelstoke Lodge Heli-Skiing
ops.region: Monashee (Gold and Pinnacle ranges) and Valhalla Range
ops.about: Private-format heli-skiing with unlimited vertical, on the old Kingfisher terrain.
ops.access: Revelstoke; airport access through Kelowna.

ops.name: Great Canadian Heli-Skiing
ops.about: Lodge right by the runs, about two down days a season on average; generous vertical with no extra charges.
ops.access: On the Trans-Canada Highway halfway between Golden and Revelstoke.

ops.name: Mustang Powder
ops.about: High remote timber lodge in a very snowy part of the Monashees. Owned by Heli (also owns Great Canadian) since 2025.
ops.access: About 2 h drive north of Kelowna to the meeting point, then into the lodge.
ops.terrain: Over 30,000 acres, 443 km of cat roads

price.t: About CAD $1,250 to $2,100 per day (older listing)

ops.name: K3 Cat Ski
ops.about: Deep powder, spaced trees and open bowls (Billy Goat Ridge, South Park, the Dark Side).
ops.access: Between Revelstoke and Sicamous.

price.t: About CAD $640 to $740 per day (older listing)

ops.name: CMH Purcell (day heli)
ops.about: The old Purcell Helicopter Skiing, now run by CMH: day heli-skiing out of Golden.
ops.access: Day lodge in Golden, about 2 h from Banff (no overnight lodge).
ops.terrain: Nearly half a million acres, 250+ runs

price.t: From about CAD $2,115 per person for one day

ops.name: CMH Bobbie Burns
ops.about: CMH lodge known for its tree skiing.
ops.access: About 2 h south of Golden; helicopter to the lodge.

ops.name: CMH Bugaboos
ops.about: Where commercial heli-skiing began in 1965, under the Bugaboo spires.
ops.access: West of Invermere; most guests fly into Calgary and take a short heli flight from near Radium Hot Springs.

ops.name: RK Heliski
ops.about: Running since 1970; gladed trees in the Jumbo Valley and high glaciated bowls.
ops.access: Resort based at Panorama, about 3 h from Calgary.
ops.terrain: 1,500 km², up to 3,000 m (some of the highest heli-skiing anywhere)

ops.name: CMH Galena
ops.about: CMH's Galena lodge in the snowy Selkirks.
ops.access: South-east of Revelstoke near Trout Lake; helicopter to the lodge.

ops.name: CMH Kootenay
ops.about: CMH's Kootenay lodge, known for tree skiing.
ops.access: Nakusp, on Upper Arrow Lake.

ops.name: Great Northern Snow-Cat Skiing
ops.about: The world's longest running owner-operated cat skiing (since 1979), about 1,500 cm of snow a year.
ops.access: About 1.5 h south of Revelstoke; drive to the lodge.
ops.level: All skiers looking for bucket-list days

price.t: 3 days from CAD $2,951 to 4 days about $4,427 per person, all-inclusive

ops.name: Stellar Heliskiing
ops.about: Small-group heli with a small-town Kootenay vibe.
ops.access: Based in Kaslo, on Kootenay Lake.

ops.name: Retallack
ops.region: Selkirk Mountains, between New Denver and Kaslo
ops.about: Up to 14+ m of snow a year, 10,000 sq ft lodge.
ops.access: On Highway 31A, between New Denver and Kaslo; about 5 h drive from Kelowna or Spokane.

price.t: About CAD $648 to $928 per day (older listing)

ops.name: Selkirk Snowcat Skiing
ops.about: The original cat skiing operation, since 1975.
ops.access: Meadow Creek, about 1.5 h drive from Nelson; snowcat ride to the lodge.

price.t: About CAD $1,040 per day (older listing)

ops.name: White Grizzly Cat Skiing
ops.about: Family-run, cozy log lodge and consistently challenging terrain, 20+ years.
ops.access: Meadow Creek, about 90 minutes from Nelson by road.

price.t: From about CAD $3,600 for a 3 day trip (older listing)

ops.name: Baldface Lodge
ops.about: Big famous cat lodge above Kootenay Lake, every kind of terrain from cruisers to steeps.
ops.access: Meet at Nelson airport, 10-minute helicopter flight to the lodge.
ops.terrain: 32,000 acres (largest cat area in the world, says Baldface)

price.t: About CAD $875 to $1,420 per day (older listing)

ops.name: Baldface Valhalla
ops.about: Baldface's day-trip tenure: high alpine, chutes, cliffs and consistent fall lines.
ops.access: Stay in Nelson and take the free shuttle to the tenure.

ops.name: Snowwater Heli Skiing
ops.about: Over 32 ft of Kootenay snow a year; cats when the heli can't fly. Sister of Valhalla Powdercats.
ops.access: Base office between Castlegar and Nelson (Highways 3A and 6); about 1 h by truck and snowcat to the lodge, about 24 km south-west of Nelson.
trips: Small group heli with snowcat backup

ops.name: Big Red Cats
ops.about: Glade and tree skiing on 8 peaks; stay at RED or in town.
ops.access: Near RED Mountain Resort, Rossland; about 2.5 h north of Spokane airport.
trips: Trips by level: intermediate, advanced, expert, pro

price.t: About CAD $649 to $719 per day (older listing)

ops.name: Island Lake Catskiing
ops.about: About 12 m of snow a year, runs to the lodge door, spa and wine.
ops.access: About 15 km from Fernie, by snowcat only; about 3.5 h drive from Calgary.
ops.lodge: Tamarack, Cedar and Red Eagle lodges

price.t: About CAD $730 to $987 per day (older listing)

ops.name: Fernie Wilderness Adventures
ops.about: Mostly single-day cat skiing since 1986: glades and chutes, plus natural jumps.
ops.access: About 20 minutes from Fernie; shuttle through Tunnel 49.
ops.terrain: About 3,000 to 5,000 acres, top drop at 2,170 m

price.t: About CAD $700 + tax per person per day

ops.name: Monashee Powder Snowcats
ops.about: About 60 ft of snow a year; first tracks 10-15 min from the lodge.
ops.access: Meet at River Ridge Golf Course on Highway 6 (about 2 h north of Kelowna); bus then cat to the lodge.

price.t: About CAD $500 to $850 per day (older listing)

ops.name: Gostlin Keefer Lake Lodge
ops.about: Steep deep trees, chutes and drops in dry interior snow.
ops.access: Near Cherryville, an easy drive from Kelowna airport.
trips: 3 and 4 day cat tours with lodging

price.t: About CAD $1,440 to $1,610 per day (older listing)

ops.name: Flowline Lodge
ops.about: Started by pro snowboarder Bjorn Leines and friends: open alpine, steep fall lines and old-growth glades.
ops.access: About 2.5 h to the meeting point; lodge at 6,400 ft.

price.t: About CAD $1,295 per day

ops.name: Chic-Chac
ops.about: Eastern Canada's cat skiing: about 7 m of snow a year in the middle of the Chic-Chocs, started in 2012 by Guillaume Molaison.
ops.access: Murdochville, Gaspésie, about 600 km north-east of Québec City. Avalanche gear included.
ops.terrain: 2 cat zones: Mont York (backcountry, 45 min cat ride) and Mont Porphyre (closer, mellower)
ops.group: Cats for 12 to 14 guests; min. 4 guests

price.t: About CAD $200 to $400 per day (older listing)

ops.name: Blomidon Cat Skiing
ops.about: Above-treeline powder on Newfoundland's west coast. We couldn't confirm it still runs: call before planning.
ops.access: Meet in Benoit's Cove, 20 minutes from Corner Brook. Phone (709) 783-2712.
trips: Single or multi-day trips (lodging not included)

price.t: About CAD $245 to $275 per day (older listing)
